comparator.name: American Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official prospective-student pages establish one coherent 180-EC American Studies pathway for the forthcoming cohort: a fixed 60-EC first year, 30 EC of fixed second-year study plus 30 EC of genuine minor space, and a third year with 20 EC of fixed specialist study, a 10-EC bachelor thesis and 30 EC of genuine free electives. The year pages identify their applicable years as 2027-2028, 2028-2029 and 2029-2030. The normalized target already names the American Studies specialisation, so that exact route is reconstructed; no neutral route choice is required.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is the American Studies specialisation within Radboud's English Language and Culture bachelor's degree. The exact named specialisation is therefore reconstructed rather than choosing between routes by reference to UCR fit.

selection.assessment: The broad closest match is complemented by two generator-backed and feasible organising directions: American literature, media and cultural expression; and American politics, identity and global affairs. Each produces material curricular consequences and exceeds the pairwise 30-EC distinctness floor, so the maximum of three alternatives is reached. The separately evidenced English-teaching direction is not feasible because UCR does not offer a sufficiently complete sequence in English linguistics, language proficiency, second-language pedagogy and supervised teacher preparation.

alternatives.label: American society, politics & culture
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines American and modern history, political institutions and international relations with sociology, literature, media, art, rhetoric, language and research; the label therefore names its broad social, political and cultural composition.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible American Studies response combines American and modern history, comparative politics, international relations, sociology, literature, media, art and rhetoric with qualitative and historical research and a psycholinguistic perspective on language.
progression: Political, rhetorical, cognitive, historical, literary, sociological and media foundations precede advanced work in American Indigenous history, race and media, contemporary social theory, persuasion, art, psycholinguistics and historical research. Introduction to Brain & Behavior precedes Psycholinguistics. Every formal prerequisite and planned-semester constraint is satisfied.

alternatives.label: American literature, media & cultural expression
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is organised around literary interpretation, American and global media, cultural history, visual art, race, rhetoric and creative production, so the label names the three dominant strands.
alternatives.concept: A humanities-led American Studies direction organised around literature, film, media, art, popular culture and creative expression, supported by American and modern history, sociology, rhetoric and interpretive research.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route removes comparative politics, international relations, peace and conflict, psycholinguistics and advanced Native American and general history. It adds media archaeology, environmental media, documentary, film-and-text study, literary theory, creative communication and advanced art-historical methods. Eight of the 24 courses differ, shifting the organising logic from a broad society-politics-culture balance to cultural interpretation and production.
progression: Introductory literature, film and media, rhetoric, modern history, art history, sociology and research methods precede advanced literary theory, film adaptation, documentary, race and media, creative communication, persuasion and art-historical research. Every course is offered in its assigned term; no selected course has an unmet formal prerequisite.

alternatives.label: American politics, identity & global affairs
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum concentrates political institutions and ideas, constitutional and international law, history, social movements, conflict, identity, race and the United States in global affairs.
alternatives.concept: A social-science and history direction centred on American political institutions, political ideas, constitutionalism, rights, identity and social conflict, with international relations, law, empire, Indigenous history, social movements and media connecting the United States to global affairs.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match, this route removes most literature, art, language and general media foundations and adds law, constitutionalism, rights, empire, social movements and youth radicalisation. Compared with the culture route, fourteen courses differ. The organising emphasis is political institutions, identity, conflict and the United States in international order.
progression: Modern history, comparative politics and Law, Society & Justice precede constitutional and international law; historical, political, sociological and research foundations precede advanced Native American history, race and media, social theory, conflict, social movements and historical research. Every formal prerequisite and planned-semester constraint is satisfied.

blocks: Modern History situates major political and social developments of the modern era, including the international setting of United States history; it is broader and less American-specific than the comparator sequence.

Histories of Gender directly studies nineteenth- to twenty-first-century American life, including slavery, gender and social experience; it covers a focused part of the broader history-and-politics course.
Both directly study settler colonialism and Indigenous North American histories, while the UCR course extends into contemporary Native American life.
Both examine international relations and the geopolitical setting of foreign policy; UCR provides general IR theory rather than a dedicated history of United States foreign relations.
Comparative Constitutional Law directly analyses the institutions, powers and legal limits that structure national political systems, including the comparative setting of American government.
UCR has no single scheduled course that provides a dedicated introduction to American Studies as an integrated field.

Both examine race, power, resistance and cultural expression in the United States; UCR's course focuses on media and systemic racism rather than the full political history of the Black freedom struggle.
UCR courses address American memory, race and identity in specific contexts, but no single scheduled course reproduces this dedicated American cultural-memory component.
UCR includes philosophical and cultural analysis across the programme but no directly equivalent Philosophy of Culture component.
Both introduce close reading and academic interpretation across literary forms and genres.
Both provide advanced literary interpretation and research; UCR is comparative and theoretical rather than a dedicated North American literature course.
Both analyse screen media and popular-cultural forms as systems of meaning, although UCR's course is a general film-and-media introduction rather than an American and British survey.
Both directly examine how media storytelling represents America and shapes understandings of its social history and everyday life.
UCR offers substantial literary study but no dedicated survey of American literature.
Both develop structured written and spoken academic communication; UCR frames those skills through rhetoric and argument.
Both analyse how linguistic choices and context shape meaning; UCR focuses on stylistics rather than the comparator's comparative-pragmatics and information-structure specialism.
Both study language scientifically; UCR provides an advanced psycholinguistic account of processing and acquisition rather than a general structural introduction.
UCR courses are taught and assessed in English, but the selected curriculum contains no dedicated English-language-proficiency writing course.
UCR develops oral communication within substantive courses but does not offer an equivalent English-language-proficiency course.
UCR does not offer a dedicated course in American English phonetics.
UCR's Psycholinguistics studies language processing and acquisition, but it does not reproduce a sociolinguistic course on English as a world language.
Both support reflection on academic development and future study or work; UCR's course is broader personal and professional formation.
The comparator preserves 30 EC of genuine minor choice space.
The comparator preserves 30 EC of genuine free elective, internship, educational-minor or study-abroad space.

notes.text: Radboud's American Studies specialisation provides a dedicated sequence in United States history and politics, American literature, media and cultural memory, English linguistics and language proficiency, followed by specialist study and a bachelor thesis. UCR can build strong programmes through American-focused courses in Native American history, gender history, media and race, combined with politics, sociology, literature, media, law and research. It does not reproduce the full American Studies sequence or the specialised English-language, phonetics and American-literature training.
